Review Text: I started using Amazon back in the 1990s as a graduate student. I purchased my textbooks there as it was cheaper than the university bookstore and tax free. Fast forward to 2008 when Amazon asked me to try prime for free. I did. And didn't realize they charged me $79 for the membership. I decided to keep it because products were cheaper than at on-ground stores, no taxes and free shipping. Then in 2012 China clamped down on counterfeit producers and stopped them from selling product in China. In 2012 Amazon opened the door to these Chinese sellers and Amazon became flooded with a bunch of junk products. The price of prime kept rising, but I kept it because of Prime video and 2-day delivery. When I became sick I relied on Amazon more. Now Amazon is expensive. They have moved lots of shows to Freevee, which I don't watch because I don't do ad TV. And to add insult to injury this year, 2024, they started adding ads to Prime Video and demanding an extra $3/month to remove the ads, citing all of the other services they added to Prime. I don't use those other services, so it is bloatware to me. Stuff isn't being delivered in 2 days anymore. And there have been times when products were lost in their shipping facilities and not delivered. You call Amazon and they outsource their customer service overseas, these people have no way to contact the drivers. This is rubbish. The seller ALWAYS has contact with shipping! Paying extra for same-day delivery doesn't guarantee it will be delivered same-day. Amazon stopped packing cushioning in boxes so I've received items damaged. I've received spoiled food items. I was horrified to learn the tea I was drinking expired months before. Once they shipped me pet food meant to be sold in Mexico. So, even though you purchase from one seller they ship the product that is closer to your domicile, which might not be the same quality. Prices aren't cheaper than the on-ground store anymore, sometimes it is higher. Taxes are included too. So there is no value to having Amazon anymore. I even submitted my SSN & 1099 to sell t-shirts on Amazon. They stopped adding people to the program that didn't have a huge social media following. But refused to delete my information from their database. Lastly, I purchased a product that was defective, a sports watch. I wanted to exchange it. The watch cost hundreds of dollars. The customer service rep wanted to offer me $25 for it. I demanded a supervisor and the US support team processed the exchange. When Hurricane Beryl was bearing down on Houston TX, I ordered the Midland NOAA radio bundle so I could be notified of tornados and floods should I lose power. My home was hit by a tornado in May 2024, so the threat was real. I paid extra for same day delivery. Amazon split the bundle with one part being delivered in a week and the other same-day, except they never delivered it and promised to deliver it AFTER the hurricane. I called and spoke to three reps. One had a fake barking dog sound and you couldn't hear a word she said. After 30 minutes she just told me to call the number I called to get her. Another promised to expedite it. He didn't. Finally I canceled the delivery with the third person. The product was sitting in Houston, I'm in Houston. I don't know why they refused to deliver it. I had to eventually purchase it from another company. This company that started out well is not the same as it was in the past when it cared about its customers. It doesn't care about its employees nor customers now, it only cares about profit. I will not be renewing my prime membership in October. And I will shop other online and on-ground retailers.

Review Text: Hands down THE best customer service I've experienced online. I'm in Denmark and have been buying goods from the German Amazon for about a decade now.I've just been given my latest refund, which was for an awful Logitech MX Keys keyboard which luckily had one of its keys fall off after about 18 months, meaning I was still under warranty. I hoped to then be able to sell the brand-new replacement for a decent amount and buy a better keyboard, but Amazon just offered a full refund, which I happily accepted.I've had returns on close to ten orders, some of which have been swiftly closed with "refund issued, no need to return the item," the others returned with a prepaid parcel slip that just needs to be printed and stuck on the box, and once they've received the item back, a refund has been issued.Once I bought twelve bottles of baby oil (enough to get free shipping), and it was delivered damaged with three bottles having escaped through a hole. I called the local carrier and was put in queue as number 90-something. While waiting I checked the Amazon website and discovered the option to have Amazon call you up. I activated it and was immediately called on my phone by an employee who promptly refunded me money for the three missing bottles, no questions asked. The local carrier called me back two hours later.This last refund was set in motion by the friendliest German supporter who laughed with me at my broken German and did his best to follow my better English.If there's one negative, it's that the search function on their own website is basically useless, so I have to use Google with "site:amazon.de" added to the query instead.I see many negative reviews based on having been fooled by refund scammers, fake websites, or forgetting your password and blaming Amazon, hating on Bezos (which I agree with), or some other random own-fault issue.I've spent at least 10k € over a decade and NEVER had a bad experience with them.People, if someone randomly calls you up and say they're from Amazon (or any other business), hang up the phone and block that number.

Review Text: VIOLATIONS OF FEDERAL FAIR TRADE COMPETITION LAW The FTC and states allege Amazon’s anticompetitive conduct occurs in two markets—the online superstore market that serves shoppers and the market for online marketplace services purchased by sellers. These tactics include:Anti-discounting measures that punish sellers and deter other online retailers from offering prices lower than Amazon, keeping prices higher for products across the internet. For example, if Amazon discovers that a seller is offering lower-priced goods elsewhere, Amazon can bury discounting sellers so far down in Amazon’s search results that they become effectively invisible.Conditioning sellers’ ability to obtain “Prime” eligibility for their products—a virtual necessity for doing business on Amazon—on sellers using Amazon’s costly fulfillment service, which has made it substantially more expensive for sellers on Amazon to also offer their products on other platforms. I seriously thought it was the best company in the world, until it wasn't.  Then it wasn't even close.  Amazon now has among the worst customer service I encounter anywhere. I no longer trust Amazon.  It's that simple.  Most recent case in point: I called Synchrony Bank, the issuer of the Amazon store card, to pay my bill.  It said the balance was over $400, so I thought I'd go through to a live person and see what the purchases were, to make sure nothing was unauthorized.  I recognized every purchase, except one.  There was an $11 charge for Amazon digital services.  I knew I hadn't authorized any digital purchases, so told them to put me through to Amazon.  The Indian man I spoke with was completely unhelpful.  Mind you, I mean him or anyone else no disrespect for being foreign.  He spoke with a thick accent likely because English was his second language.  GOOD FOR HIM.  It's something to be proud of.  But it also makes it very difficult to take care of issues that have any degree of complexity at all. He insisted I definitely ordered Amazon Music Unlimited, because I played [unintelligible] on my Alexa device.  What was the name of it?  "It was [unintelligible]"  HUH?  SAY THAT AGAIN SLOWLY?  Literally, his accent was so thick I couldn't tell at all what he was saying.  After repeating it a fourth time, I made out the word "noise."  It hit me that Amazon was charging me $11 a month to play "brown noise" on my bedroom Alexa device.  I've played that as a background sleep noise for YEARS.  Didn't start in December.  I've literally played it for about 3-5 years, every single night.  Suddenly it apparently started charging me for it in December.  I never heard it ask me ANYTHING about a subscription and certainly never agreed to any such thing.  But that didn't convince this Amazon rep, who apparently could read my mind and insisted I absolutely did order it.  I grew increasingly annoyed, especially as he kept going silent for 20, 30, 40 seconds at a time without saying a word, no hold or anything.. just silence.  Finally I told him, "why are you being silent?  I don't know what you're doing."  He then hung up on me.  So much for customer service.  I called angrier now and spoke with a second rep. She puts me on hold... and I wait and I wait and wait some more.  About 15 minutes she comes back and says "I'm sorry for the long wait.  I'm still in the queue to speak with Amazon music."  I told her I would wait.  She puts me back on hold... 20 minutes pass... 30 minutes pass... 40 minutes pass.  Finally I had to give up.  She never came back on the line to say anything.  Just the same canned music playing over and over and over and over on a loop.  Called again.  Asked for a supervisor, but my phone died because I'd been held on the line so long.  He didn't call back.  I gave up because I had to give up.  Otherwise, I'd have a stroke from my anger and high blood pressure.  Amazon, you suck. Every single time I have a problem now, this is what I encounter.  Amazon is no longer a great company.  It's a company that will cut every corner, that disrespects its customers and their time, and that cares only about its bottom line.  It will go the way of Sears because it deserves to.

I was attempting to access my account to make a purchase, and upon reaching the login page and entering my credentials, the following message appeared: ‘Your account has been terminated for improper use of Amazon services. We have sent you an email with more information.’ (It was written in Italian, I translated it with Google translate). However, no email arrived in my inbox despite repeated attempts. I began searching online to see if anyone else had encountered the same issue. I found an email address where I could file a complaint. Following termination of your account due to breach of contract, you are not permitted to open a new account or use another account to place orders on our site. Following a thorough evaluation, we have decided not to restore your full access to this account. It will therefore not be possible for you to place orders on our site. Any digital content purchased with this account is still available to you. Here arises an interesting question: how did they learn that my account was closed if my device was not connected to Wi-Fi? This implies that Amazon has another means of controlling my data and my device. All the books I downloaded, all the notes I made in the books, all the progress I made (I usually read several books at the same time) - everything was gone! An empty Kindle!!!I am deeply disappointed and angry with the situation and feel utterly helpless in resolving this problem. My account was canceled without explanation, I cannot ask questions through the app's customer service as my account is closed, Amazon support has ceased responding to my emails, my Kindle books have been deleted, and there is no one who seems to care or can offer assistance in any way to address this issue.

Review Text: It's hard to know where to start because there is now so much wrong with this company's services.Having been an Amazon Prime customer for well over a decade I have seen a lot of changes but recently the service has gone downhill to the point that I will not be renewing my subscription when it next expires.Particular issues that I've experiences are:1. Fake products - There are now a large number of cheap/dangerous knockoff products on amazon and it is impossible to tell from the listings which are genuine and which are the fakes.2. Reviews - The review system is broken and now so full of fake and even fraudulent reviews it has lost all meaning. Basic tricks like aggregating reviews for several products or even switching reviews over to a completely different product are common and no attempt seems to be made to stop this practice.3. Prime Delivery - This increased significantly in price and whereas once next day delivery was the norm, the minimum I am now quoted is 3 to 5 days with most items not even despatching for a couple of days after the order - as bad as the free delivery for non-prime members. It is not unusual for items to take two to three weeks to arrive despite paying the Prime premium.I am also seeing a lot of instances where the item goes to "collected by courier" status very quickly preventing order cancellation but no further movement or valid training information appears for several days suggesting that the item has probably not actually been despatched and that status change was just to stop me cancelling when I discover the delay.4. Prime Video - This was always a bit of a rip-off with most items incurring an extra charge on top of prime membership but the latest change forces you to pay an extra subscription on top of the already expensive Prime membership to get the add free viewing I got for free up until now.5. Prime music - this is another service that has been deliberately made almost unusable unless you want to pay yet another addition subscription on top.6. Customer services - All contact is via chat or phone, not email, so hard to make formal complaints or keep a paper trail. Although occasionally helpful, most of the time they merely read information to you that you can already see on the website and promises of action are rarely followed through.I have, at one point or another raised all of these issues with Amazon customer services only to be met with responses that ranged from complete indifference to promises to pass on my concerns which clearly went no further because nothing changed.In short, other than the convenience of having so many items in one place there is little to commend this company any more. Amazon Prime in particular is most definitely no longer worth the money.

Review Text: BUYER BEWARE. As a Prime Member, Amazon did NOT make good on an order even though they didn't follow delivery instructions asked for at the time of order. As a result, and as a possible theft, Amazon did NOT provide a refund or replacement order even after completing every required step stated by reps. Also, as in my case, you will never speak to the same rep again. Even after your claim reportedly goes to “escalation,” you must call the general customer service number and start over, which includes reexplaining EVERYTHING as if it’s the first time you called. He said our claim would be resolved quickly after he sent all to Escalation and not to worry about the deadline since we had completed everything required by that date. Yet on the “deadline date,” I called and spoke to 2 reps. I was told by the first rep after placing me on an extended hold, that he had called the police department and they had no record of a report from me on file, therefore there was nothing Amazon could do.  I again explained I had sent a PDF of a Sheriff’s Department report due to law enforcement jurisdiction as instructed by the local police department three times! He just repeated the same thing again with no acknowledgement of what I just said.  I begged him to listen and not hang up. I asked what "police" number he had called to verify he had called the Sheriff's Department; he said he couldn’t share that information due to privacy. I verbally stated the phone number of the Sheriff’s Department and asked if he had called that number - he wouldn't answer. I then asked to speak to his supervisor and was assured the supervisor would give me the same information he had. After an extended hold, someone new got on the phone. With a rude demeanor, he repeated that they had no police report on file; therefore, there would be no further support – refund or reorder. When I insisted it was there, again explaining that the jurisdiction was with the Sheriff’s office, he stated it did not contain all the information required. With witness at my side, I asked repeatedly for him to provide specifics of what was not included as I had referred to their email requirements, emailed those requirements to the Sheriff's Department, and saw the report with my own eyes, confirming all requirements met. Bottomline: I have wasted significant time and effort – for nothing. I’ve taken a big financial loss on goods not delivered and paid at the same time a Prime Member fee to experience this type of treatment. (I also unfortunately ended up in the ER due to the stress of this all with heart issues.) Almost humorous, as you are on hold, Amazon’s recording speaks of their desire to have the best world class service. I am not a rude or unreasonable person. I used to be the Sr. V.P. in charge of customer service for a large company where we strived to protect the company but be fair with our customers. Trust me, Amazon's service is the worst. It’s inexcusable and I’m surprised there hasn’t been a class action lawsuit over inconsistent and unfair practices. Even if you’ve heard positive things about Amazon or you haven't had a problem yourself, just wait. Your turn may be coming. And it may be a horrific experience like mine.

Review Text: Two items that I ordered on Amazon were never delivered, and when I look at the order status on Amazon, it says "Your package may be lost."  This has happened a number of times with other orders.  I called Customer Service to get my lost items replaced, and I spoke with a rep who was nice and polite, but I simply could not understand what she was saying to me.  I had to ask her to repeat what she was saying many, many times, and when she did, I often still could not understand her.  I realize that providing overseas customer support has financial advantages for Amazon, but it is at the expense of customers.  On almost every customer service call I have made to Amazon, I have had a great deal of trouble communicating with the rep.  And I have often received information that is completely incorrect.  I remember when Customer Service reps were based in the U.S., and they were great and I was able to communicate with them.  My heart sinks every time I have to call Customer Service and I hear someone answer with a heavy accent because I know the interaction is going to be difficult and stressful.  I love  Amazon because of their huge and varied inventory and the ease of ordering from them, but I hate their Customer Service and Amazon delivery services.  Before Amazon created their own delivery service and delivery was handled by Fedex and UPS and a few others, I never had a problem with delivery.  But now I've had multiple problems, with my items being delivered to the wrong address (when my address is clearly posted on my house), with my items not being delivered at all but being "lost," and with my items being delivered late.  I miss the old Amazon and have definite mixed feelings about the current one.

Review Text: I ordered an IPad Air from Amazon (the company itself rather than a Marketplace seller) on 24th November. It was meant to be my daughter’s Christmas present and it cost several hundred pounds. It should have been delivered to me on 26th November, though instead I was delivered a box of opened dry cat food. I presume that an Amazon employee somewhere along the chain took the IPad and replaced it with the cat food that they emptied to an equivalent weight.I phoned Amazon Customer Services on 26th November and explained what had happened. I asked I be sent an actual IPad Air, though was told I could only be refunded the money, and only once Amazon had “received my return” (the cat food). UPS collected the cat food from me on 27th and delivered it to Amazon on 28th November.Two and a half weeks and several phone calls to Amazon down the line I was told today that “hopefully” I should be refunded my money on 3rd January 2024 (38 days after I’d initially explained to Amazon what had happened and “returned” the item).Each Amazon Customer Services person over the past couple of weeks has treated me indifferently, as if I’m a customer who has returned an unwanted book rather than someone who has essentially been defrauded by an Amazon employee. In actual fact I’ve been treated worse than someone returning an unwanted book, as if it had been a low cost item that was being refunded I would have been reimbursed within 14 days, rather than it taking more than a month because of the financial cost involved. I have kept on being told to “be patient” and that I’ll be refunded in 5 to 10 days, though the date keeps being put back for no reason that anyone has explained, and now for some reason I won’t be refunded until 2024. It means my daughter will be without a Christmas present this year. No one at Amazon seems particularly bothered or sympathetic.I might continue to buy inexpensive items from Amazon that I can’t easily get elsewhere, though I certainly won’t be buying anything expensive from them again. Though buying from Amazon is often convenient, it is much safer to shop with a retailer with decent, accessible and relatively transparent Customer Services.

But the saving grace was their customer service would fix your issues. That is NO longer the case. Customer service will instead try to do anything they can to not refund you for a package lost in shipping (even with tracking!) or a return. Every time you talk to a representative you will hear something completely different. They have no clue what they are doing, they just want you off the phone/chat ASAP.I will never use Amazon again, after 18 years and $15,000+ PER year spent, they will never get another cent from me. Ordering anything from them is now stressful because you anticipate something will go wrong. Try literally ANY other site. Want electronics? B&H. Want regular goods? Target or Walmart. Trading cards or art? eBay or Etsy. Literally anything but Amazon. I never thought I would dump Amazon, but it is now far more trouble than it’s worth. If it continues on this track, Prime will be removed as a service in the next few years.

Review Text: I have been posting book reviews on Amazon for many years, always buying the books at the site to get the cachet of “Verified purchase”. My efforts resulted in more than thirty reviews appearing on Amazon, many rated as either “Top Positive Review” or “Top Critical Review”. But when I submitted a review of “The Last Politician” by Franklin Foer, I got a terse email from Amazon that it could not be posted “because it doesn’t meet our guidelines for one or more of these reasons: Profanity, Harassment, Hate Speech, Sexual Content, Illegal Activity, Private Information”. This had never happened before, and I was quite surprised. I went to the link that showed the “Community Guidelines” and read all six pages, scratching my head, trying to figure what I’d done wrong and then I realized the issue was politics. The person checking my review was apparently an extreme liberal so I made some changes that I thought might let my piece “pass” and I resubmitted it. But I soon realized this was a waste of time because I could make changes piecemeal again and again, but without knowing exactly what in my 850 word review was the ”problem”, my efforts would be fruitless.How could I get the nameless and faceless Amazon person behind the “wizard’s curtain” to tell me what to do? I remembered seeing on my “Author’s Page” a place where I could recommend books. I’d never used this feature before but now got the idea to cite Franklin Foer’s book as a “Recommendation”, writing in the comments, “I wrote a review of this book that did not pass the Amazon Moderator and I hope they will tell me what to change.” This was an act of desperation because I truly wanted to get my review posted and I was willing to make rewrites but had to have some guidance, sort of like we got from our high school English teacher who would take a red pencil and underline the problem.Apparently, my ploy with Amazon backfired because I soon got an email saying my post was “outside of our guidelines” and “consider this to be a first warning.” Amazon’s ire was about the book recommendation I’d put on my author’s page (specifically the comments showing Amazon in a bad light) since this was the only “post” I’d ever made other than book reviews.This was going nowhere, and I was not going to play Amazon’s games. I replied to the email, saying, “if you cannot tell me what I am doing wrong I will cancel my book advertising, Amazon Prime, and the Amazon prime credit card and quit making purchases from Amazon.” Six days later I got a reply email saying, “You have repeatedly posted content that violates our Community Guidelines . . . [and therefore] we’ve removed your ability to participate in Community features.” This was untrue because I’d only made one post, the one where I said, “I hope they [Amazon Moderator] will tell me what to change [in the review that had been rejected].”Unfortunately, all the book reviews I’d posted on Amazon over the years were deleted. This was quite disappointing because I’d spent hundreds of dollars on dozens of books, reading them closely over countless hours in order to write honest and informed book reviews and now my work had come to naught. I truly doubt that anyone has put more effort(both in the reading and the writing) into creating a book review than I have. Amazon’s actions have not only hurt me but are a disservice to millions of readers who rely on quality reviews to make wise decisions in their book purchases.As I said earlier, I’ve submitted critical assessments of other books to Amazon and never had a problem and I must conclude the current issue is over politics, simply having a different opinion. While I did say some positives about the author, I also faulted him for being almost sycophantic toward Biden. What he wrote was an uncritical fluff piece and I called it as such. The review, as written, would be passable to any reasonable person and there is nothing out of bounds in it. I read the book thoroughly and wrote an honest, critical review with no malice or evil intent. For anyone interested, a google search of “book reviews of ‘The Last Politician’” will take you to Goodreads where you’ll find my piece and you can decide for yourself.

I find more and more these days so many high street brand stores often only provide top selling products with limited to zero choices being readily made available to the consumer and that includes their internet shopping sites. Time after time I’ve visited many of these companies and then swiftly moved across to Amazon. Being with Amazon the opposite is true, so many wide ranging products, such huge variety, so many obscure products, and the opportunity to shop at my convenience at anytime day or night so for these reasons thats why Amazon always tends getting my money and vote. Review Text: Dissatisfied with Amazon's Recent Policies and ServiceI have been a loyal Amazon customer for many years, but recent experiences have left me deeply dissatisfied with the company's policies and service. I want to emphasize that my dissatisfaction is not directed at any specific representative but is primarily related to systemic issues stemming from Amazon's new policies.​ Incorrect Items Received: On multiple occasions, I have received the wrong items in my orders. These mistakes not only caused inconvenience but also resulted in wasted time and resources as I had to arrange returns and replacements.​ Items Not Received and Police Report: One incident stands out where a package mysteriously disappeared. I had to file a police report due to the significant value of the missing items. This was an extremely distressing experience and raises concerns about Amazon's delivery and security measures.​ Items Delivered to the Wrong Address: I have also faced situations where items were marked as "delivered" but were, in reality, delivered to the wrong address. This forced me to engage in a time-consuming process to track down and retrieve my packages.​ Refund Delays: The most frustrating aspect of my recent interactions with Amazon has been the extensive delays in processing refunds. Waiting for 30 to 60 days for a refund is not just an inconvenience but also feels like a tactic akin to withholding customer funds.​ This pattern of behavior resembles actions taken by financial institutions to retain customers' money rather than providing satisfactory customer service. It is disheartening to witness Amazon, a company I once held in high regard, resorting to such practices.​ As a result of these recurring issues and my growing frustration, I have made the difficult decision to discontinue my patronage of Amazon. While I have enjoyed the convenience and variety of products offered in the past, the recent decline in service quality and the apparent disregard for customer satisfaction have left me with no choice.​ I hope that by sharing my experiences, Amazon will take the necessary steps to address these issues and improve its customer service. It is my belief that companies should prioritize customer satisfaction over all else, as loyal customers are the lifeblood of any business.​ In conclusion, I can no longer place my trust in Amazon as a reliable online shopping platform, and I will be seeking alternatives for my future purchases.

This has been a frustrating and disappointing experience.   I have been somewhat of an Amazon junkie for several years now.   I tell my coworkers, "If you can't find it on Amazon,  it doesn't exist.".  I've experienced prompt deliveries most of the time. A few late ones now and again, but this one is strange.
